name: Grains & Noodles
tagline: Pasta, rice, soba, udon, couscous, millet, quinoa. Staple foods from every tradition, evaluated for origin, variety, and production method.

learn.how_we_evaluate: In this category, origin and production method are the primary signals. We look for named grain varieties, disclosed grain origin (separate from pasta origin), and honest production claims. Bronze-die extrusion and slow low-temperature drying are meaningful quality signals for pasta — but only when the producer can actually demonstrate them. Organic certification matters here because glyphosate use as a pre-harvest desiccant is common in conventional grain farming.
what_to_look_for: Named grain variety (Senatore Cappelli, Saragolla, durum semolina, etc.)
Grain origin disclosed separately from pasta production origin
Bronze-die extrusion (trafilatura al bronzo) for pasta
Slow low-temperature drying (below 50°C, 12–56 hours) for pasta
Organic certification or published glyphosate-free test results
red_flags: No grain variety mentioned — generic 'durum wheat semolina' only
'Made in Italy' with no grain origin — grain may be from Canada or elsewhere
Teflon-die extrusion not disclosed (smooth, shiny surface is a visual indicator)
Organic claimed without EU BIO or equivalent certification mark

key_terms.definition: Pasta extruded through a bronze die has a rough, porous surface that holds sauce better. Slower and more expensive than Teflon extrusion. The artisan standard.

Indicazione Geografica Protetta / Protected Geographical Indication. Links a product to a specific place. Pasta di Gragnano IGP means the pasta was produced exclusively in Gragnano using defined methods.
Integrated supply chain. When the same producer controls grain growing, milling, and pasta production. The highest level of traceability available in this category.

An ancient durum wheat variety selected in the early 20th century. Lower yield but higher protein and often higher digestibility than modern commercial varieties. A meaningful transparency signal when named on packaging.
